children: Egypt's annual headline inflation rate is expected to have accelerated to 15.5% in August from 14.9% in July, driven by unfavourable base effects and higher electricity tariffs, a Reuters poll conducted between September 1 and 8 found.
The median forecast of 17 analysts was for annual urban consumer inflation to rise to 15.5% in August. Forecasts ranged from 14.6% to 16.3%.
The government statistics agency CAPMAS is due to release the data on Thursday, September 10.

"We expect Egypt's headline inflation rate to increase from 14.9% y/y in July to 16.3% y/y in August," said James Swanston at Barclays, who had the highest forecast, citing unfavourable base effects and the impact of the late-July electricity tariff hike.
Daniel Richards at Emirates NBD said that August would likely mark the peak, with base effects turning more favourable in the second half.

Farouk Soussa at Goldman Sachs, whose 15.2% forecast was towards the lower end of the range, said inflation was likely to remain near current levels before easing in the first quarter of 2027. That trajectory should allow the central bank to keep interest rates on hold at 19% for the rest of the year before resuming an easing cycle in 2027, with rates falling to 13% in the first quarter of 2028, he said.
Five analysts also provided forecasts for core inflation. The median estimate was 14.7%, unchanged from July, with forecasts ranging from 14.5% to 15.5%.

Egypt has been gradually removing fuel and electricity subsidies under commitments linked to its $8 billion International Monetary Fund support package. The measures have repeatedly fed through to consumer prices, even as headline inflation has fallen from a record 38% in September 2023.
